job.rawJd: Job Title: Senior UX Designer. Location: Remote. Who We Are: HMH is a learning technology company committed to delivering connected solutions that engage learners, empower educators, and improve student outcomes. As a leading provider of K-12 core curriculum, supplemental and intervention solutions and professional learning services, HMH partners with educators and school districts to uncover solutions that unlock students' potential and extend teachers' capabilities. HMH serves more than 50 million students and 4 million educators in 150 countries. What You'll Do: The Senior UX Designer will help create world class, accessible digital experiences for educational software. In this role, you'll collaborate closely with product and engineering partners to solve complex problems and deliver accessible, user centered solutions reporting to the Senior Design Manager. Responsibilities: Lead UX and product design efforts from concept through final execution using Figma. Design intuitive, high-quality experiences that meet user needs, business goals, and technical requirements. Apply accessibility best practices and WCAG compliance standards across all design work. Leverage user research, data, and insights to inform and validate design decisions. Collaborate with cross-functional partners to define problems, explore solutions, and iterate on designs. Participate in product and design meetings to contribute ideas and solve complex product challenges. Present and clearly articulate design concepts, rationale, and tradeoffs to stakeholders. Use AI tools appropriately to improve efficiency, streamline workflows, and support smarter ways of working. Produce user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and detailed design specifications. Ensure alignment with design systems, UX standards, and established patterns. What You'll Need: Bachelor's degree in Design or related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 3-5+ years of UX design experience working on collaborative teams. A portfolio that shows a strong understanding of the complete UX design process, from research to final design. Proficiency in Figma and modern UX design tools. Proven ability to design accessible, user-friendly, and inclusive digital experiences. Role Expectations: Work independently as well as collaborate with cross functional teams. Attend meetings and actively participate in team reviews and product discussions. Develop a strong understanding of the product to deliver thoughtful, effective solutions. Salary range: $95,000-$103,000. Application Deadline: The application window for this position is anticipated to close on July 24, 2026. The posting may be available past this date but is not guaranteed. HMH is fully committed to Equal Employment Opportunity and to attracting, retaining, developing and promoting the most qualified employees without regard to protected characteristics. HMH is dedicated to a work environment free from discrimination and harassment and actively participates in E-Verify.

unsupportedRequirements: Direct K-12 or educational-software product-design employment is not shown; the posting describes HMH's domain but does not make prior education experience a requirement.
Formal WCAG certification or dedicated accessibility-auditor ownership is not shown.
The portfolio does not isolate detailed design-specification documents as a standalone artifact, although it shows build-ready systems, interaction guidance, and engineering handoff.
missingEvidence: No case study is centered on student, teacher, curriculum, or school-district users.
The application should not imply formal accessibility certification or direct edtech tenure.

coverLetterBridge.rationale: This is a direct portfolio-primary UX fit. The selected work already demonstrates the full process HMH asks for—research, Figma, accessible system direction, complex product UX, cross-functional iteration, and final execution—so a cover letter is not needed to make the core case.

fitGate.recommendation: Proceed as strong. Lead with research-to-execution product UX, accessible design-system work, Figma-based collaboration, and senior cross-functional ownership. Treat K-12 as a domain to learn rather than claimed prior experience, and do not overstate accessibility certification.
